title: Striking the Right Balance: Recall Loss for Semantic Segmentation
mechanism: Weight CE per class by (1 - running recall), interpolating between plain CE and inverse-frequency CE, so under-called classes get more weight only while they are under-called.
adaptation: EMA recall per class across batches (splice absent from most batches of 8). Targets gridline recall 0.33 and splice recall 0. Follow with per-class post-hoc bias to recover precision lost.
min_experiment: Arm: recall-weighted CE + Dice(crack, inactive), 3 seeds, then OOF bias; baseline SUP100 and R2c; metric gridline IoU and mIoU_rob; kill if gridline IoU not above 0.357 (R2c) or mIoU_rob < +0.01.
evidence: R: Synthia, DeepLab-ResNet18: +9% relative mean accuracy with competitive mIoU.
prior_overlap: Partial: Dice on gridline (R2c) already showed recall gain at precision cost (gridline 0.283 -> 0.357, mIoU_rob n.d.). Recall-weighted CE across all classes not tested.
